subject: Re: Redwood discovery - EU data residency & security next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Luca Moretti <luca.moretti@eurofintech.eu>

Subject: Re: Redwood discovery - EU data residency & security next steps

Hi Anna / Luca,

Thanks again for the time today — great to learn more about EuroFintech's EU rollout and the compliance checks you need before procurement. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from today's call:
- SOC 2: you asked whether Redwood has a SOC 2 report and whether we can provide a redacted copy.
- GDPR / HIPAA: you need confirmation on GDPR controls and whether Redwood can support HIPAA (BAA required) for regulated workloads.
- Vendor security questionnaire: you mentioned sending over a short Vendor SecQ and asked for a target return date.
- Data residency & cross-border: primary ask — can data be kept in the EU (Dublin/Frankfurt) with no cross-border transfers for regulated data?
- Export controls (OFAC/ITAR): you asked whether we block specific geographies or restricted exports and what our screening controls are.

What I can share right away:
- Attached: Redwood Security factsheet (high-level) and our standard DPA template.
- SOC 2: we maintain a SOC 2 Type II report; I will share a redacted copy for vendor review.
- Regions: we operate EU regions (Dublin and Frankfurt). By default customer-controlled data for EU accounts is kept in-region.
- Cross-border transfers: we support contractual controls and region-locking for production workloads; we can discuss contractual language (DPA + SCCs or EU adequacy mechanisms if needed).
- OFAC/ITAR: we perform customer screening and have controls to prevent processing for sanctioned parties. For ITAR/defense-restricted data we recommend Private deployments with on-prem or VPC options.

Next steps / asks:
1) Please send the Vendor Security Questionnaire when convenient — target return date would be Fri 2026-02-28 if that works for your procurement timeline.
2) I will loop in our security SME and solutions engineer (cc'ed) to answer detailed technical questions and send the redacted SOC 2 and DPA.
3) If helpful, let's schedule a 30-minute compliance deep-dive next week (I've linked a Calendly in the footer).

Attaching the factsheet now.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Security_Factsheet_2026.pdf (PDF)]

2) Please send your DPA template and tell us whether Redwood supports SCCs / EU adequacy mechanisms by default for EU accounts.
3) For cross-border transfers: our legal team requires that certain data classes (PII for EU customers) remain in-region with no outbound transfer without explicit contractual permission. Is region-locking available as a contractual guarantee?
4) Attached is our vendor security questionnaire — we'd appreciate return by 2026-02-28 if possible.
5) OFAC/ITAR: please confirm whether you run sanctions screening and whether there are any restrictions we should be aware of for cross-border services.

Attaching the vendor questionnaire. Happy to do a quick call next week with our security lead if needed.

Subject: Re: Redwood discovery - EU data residency & security next steps

Anna — thanks, and appreciate the vendor questionnaire. Looping in Dylan (SE) and Rishi (Security) to provide the details below and to coordinate the questionnaire return. 

Quick answers up front (will follow with attachments):
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II in August 2024. I have a redacted PDF; attaching now for vendor review.
- DPA & SCCs: attaching our DPA template. We support SCCs and other adequacy mechanisms; our standard DPA covers EU data residency controls and export contract terms.
- Region-locking: Yes — for EU accounts we can configure region-locking for production workloads and apply contractual language in the DPA to restrict cross-border processing for designated data classes.
- OFAC/ITAR: We perform sanctions screening at onboarding and maintain policies to block sanctioned entities. For ITAR or other export-controlled technical data, we recommend Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) and can provide options for air-gapped/offline workflows.

Attachments included: SOC2 redacted, DPA template, and the security factsheet I sent earlier.

Proposed next step: Dylan / Rishi — can you confirm the technical controls (encryption KMS options, region-locking implementation details) and confirm whether we can produce an export-controls attestation for procurement?

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Anna — quick technical follow-up from SE: 

Encryption & keys:
- All customer data is encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest (AES-256).
- For Hosted customers we provide platform-managed keys by default; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) and HSM integrations.

Region-locking & egress controls:
- EU regions (eu-west-1/Dublin, eu-central-1/Frankfurt) are available and can be configured so that processing, storage, and backups remain within the selected region.
- We can disable automatic cross-region replication for regulated accounts and apply strict egress rules.

Export controls / screening:
- We run OFAC screening during onboarding and block accounts that match sanctions lists.
- For ITAR/data subject to export controls we recommend Private deployments; we can provide a short attestation note for procurement describing our screening and restrictions. If EuroFintech needs additional contractual language, Rishi can advise on specific clauses.

I can also pull together a short technical appendix (1-2 pages) summarizing these controls for your security team. Would Friday 2026-02-26 for questionnaire return and deep-dive on Mon 2026-03-01 work?

Cheers,
Dylan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
